column2: The feeling of acute secondhand embarrassment for others' (and sometimes your own) actions.
The atmosphere, mood, or energy radiated by a place, a person, or a track.
A man over thirty who has given up on his appearance and loves beer, the couch, and video games.
A girl with a bright alternative look, memes in her head, and heavy boots.
A good-looking guy who turns out to be a toxic manipulator.
The perfect caring TikTok boyfriend who always pays the bill and covers you with a blanket.
Just some random guy or acquaintance whose name doesn't really matter.
Psychological violence in relationships, a trend word for all zoomers with therapy experience.
The art of convincing your partner that they imagined everything and are to blame themselves.
A person you secretly or openly pine for but are afraid to approach.
Fantasizing about a romantic relationship between two characters or acquaintances.
Bragging about a new iPhone, clothes, or just having a great time to the beat.
A joke or prank you laugh at until you cry (sometimes exclusively at yourself).
A person who, in response to a joke, starts tediously explaining why it's scientifically incorrect.
The point of view of the video's author, where the viewer must imagine themselves in their place.
The highest praise for a flawless look, action, or incredible charisma.
A lone wolf with a stone face who keeps to himself and doesn't care about the crowd's opinion.
A state of slight detachment from reality when you live in your own pink fantasies.
Natural charm and the ability to smoothly flirt without a single awkward word.
Suddenly disappearing from a conversation without explanation, like a ghost.
A sandy planet where Timothée Chalamet rides giant worms for spice.
A gloomy girl with braids whose dance in a black dress was replicated by the entire internet.
A film about the creator of the atomic bomb that came out the same day as Barbie and spawned 'Barbenheimer.'
A series with Zendaya about high school drama, glitter under the eyes, and complicated addictions.
A gritty series where superheroes aren't world saviors but cynical and cruel corporate stars.
A visual masterpiece from Netflix based on the League of Legends game with a soundtrack by Imagine Dragons.
A ninja forever running with his arms flung back, dreaming of becoming Hokage.
Dark fantasy about a swordsman with a huge blade, read for its harsh masculine drama.
A cult modern anime about sorcerers, curses, and the white-haired sensei Satoru Gojo.
The name of the protagonist of Fight Club, whose quotes are still used as profile pictures.
A Nolan space drama whose music makes even those who don't know physics cry.
Hollywood's main curly-haired crush, who played both Paul Atreides and Willy Wonka.
The actress without whom no major premiere or red carpet seems to happen these days.
The actor who 'didn't die at the end of Drive' and became the face of memes about lonely men.
A green ogre from a swamp who turned from a cartoon character into a genuine internet religion.
A stop-motion film about a girl who finds a world where her parents have buttons instead of eyes.
A childhood cartoon series in which, as an adult, you suddenly discover deep philosophy.
A director who loves blowing up real planes and making viewers' brains explode over time.
A director whose films feature lots of dialogue, blood, and obligatory close-ups of women's feet.
The boy with the scar whose school houses zoomers still use to determine their personality.
A blocky world where you can build anything from Hogwarts to a working computer out of redstone.
A platform where millions of teens create their own games and spend pocket money on skins.
A team game where you can learn a lot about your parents from strangers on your team.
The legendary shooter (Counter-Strike) where the main skill remains throwing smoke on time and not 'throwing the match.'
A beautiful anime game for whose new characters players are ready to sell their soul (and salary).
The monster hunter Geralt, who constantly grumbles, hates portals, and loves playing Gwent.
A game about the future city of Night City, where rocker Keanu Reeves moves into the protagonist's head.
A game people have been playing for fifteen years but still haven't reached the main plot.
The main streaming platform where people watch other people play games or just eat.
The messenger of all gamers, without whose voice channels no evening raid is complete.
A digital game store where during sales people buy dozens of games they'll never launch.
A mobile action game (Brawl Stars) that every schoolkid in the country used to grind during breaks.
A life simulator where it's easier to build a mansion with a pool without stairs than in reality.
A fighting game in which everyone since childhood tries to remember the button combo for a fatality.
A football simulator that has caused more broken gamepads than all other games combined.
A crime simulator whose sixth installment humanity awaits more eagerly than a Mars landing.
A game about a space crew that taught a whole generation to lie masterfully to friends' faces.
A person whose job is to sit in front of a webcam, joke, and read donations from viewers.
A dishonest player with software who ruins the mood for all other match participants.
A virtual 'kinder surprise' in games that almost always drops junk.
The singer Swift, whose fans' influence can rival a small army.
The singer Billie, who proved you can become a superstar by recording whispers in a bedroom with your brother.
The Canadian singer with a palm-tree hairstyle in the past and a main hit about 'blinding lights.'
A genius producer and the main supplier of the strangest news and fashion scandals.
The rapper Scott, whose concerts feel like earthquakes and whose sneakers cost as much as a plane wing.
A genre of aggressive electronic music used in internet edits of night drifts and workouts.
Korean pop music with flawless choreography and fans ready to tear anyone apart for their idol.
A streaming service whose year-end results absolutely everyone posts in their stories in December.
A program that makes your voice sound cosmic and lets even the tone-deaf sing.
A sped-up or slowed-down version of an old song that gets a second life on social media.
A joint track by two artists, for which even sworn rivals team up.
Artificial intelligence that now writes diplomas instead of students and draws cats with six legs.
The main digital tutor and co-author of all term papers of the last two years.
A smart AI companion who knows about the Princes of Amber, about skoofs, and can even pretend it had nothing to do with it.
An app with an endless feed of short videos where five minutes imperceptibly turn into three in the morning.
A messenger that has become for young people simultaneously a news feed, a social network, and a cloud.
A social network where people save pictures of beautiful rooms and outfits they'll never bring to life.
A bright green Japanese powdered tea with coconut milk — the favorite drink of aesthetes.
What teenagers are ready to save their stipend for months to get the logo of on a hoodie.
Clothing three sizes too big, in which it's cozy to hide from the outside world and the cold.
A particular visual style or atmosphere for which people pick filters, clothes, and even tea mugs.
A state where you're twenty and already tired of work, studies, and life itself.
Regular visits to a psychologist, which modern youth are prouder of than a new phone.
The trendy ability to understand your feelings in the moment and not snap at others.
A warning sign in a person's behavior after which it's best to run from the date immediately.
A sign of a healthy and adequate person who can listen and doesn't disappear for a week.
Sweet tea with tapioca pearls drunk through a super-wide straw.
The brick of life without which leaving home with a charged battery counts as extreme sports.
A talk-based audio show convenient to listen to while washing dishes or riding the subway.
A representative of the generation to which this crossword is dedicated and who will definitely guess all these words.
